jobs.title: Country Head of People Experience – Japan
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

The Country Head of People Experience is the P&O leader who carries full accountability for all P&O-related experiences in a country and is responsible for local execution of business and people strategies where this impacts the local workforce, covering all business units that operate out of that country – to the business, to employees, and to external parties including regulatory bodies, works councils, and trade unions. The role partners closely with the global and local P&O Workforce Strategy Heads to understand the local business strategies and to identify how best to support the implementation of people related strategies. The local P&O Workforce Strategy Head is the primary contact for the local Business Leader.

This is the role that local leaders and (local/ global) P&O Workforce Strategy Heads turn to for guidance on country-specific P&O practices, for escalation of complex people matters that require local legal or regulatory authority, and for trusted guidance on the local context in which their respective business strategies must be executed. The role works in close partnership with Global & Local P&O Workforce Strategy Heads to translate business and P&O strategy into actionable, locally grounded plans — and is accountable for the implementation of that people experience strategy on the ground.

Alongside this strategic execution responsibility, the role ensures that global P&O products and programs land in ways that are legally compliant, culturally resonant, and genuinely adopted by employees and managers. It is the keeper of the lived people experience in-country — ensuring that what is designed globally is experienced well locally, across every moment that matters. The role provides input to People Experience Product Owners in case of issues or needs to adapt to local realities.

In a federated P&O model where global product teams and global business-aligned Expertise Hub partners each play distinct roles, the Country Head of People Experience is the integrating force on the ground: the single point of accountability for P&O in-country, and the organization's most authoritative voice when local law, practice, or context requires a considered response.

Job Description

• Global ‘Country People Experience’ Leadership Team Member Key and active member of the Global ‘Country People Experience’ Leadership Team, together defining and driving the Novartis Country People Experience ambition, strategy and enterprise priorities.

• Local P&O Accountability to the Business & External Parties This is the most fundamental accountability of the role and the one that distinguishes it from any purely product or operational function. The Country Head of People Experience is the single point of P&O accountability across all units in the country for local P&O practices and policies or in-country delivery of (relevant) P&O related products — to local business leaders who need P&O authority, to regulatory bodies that require a named responsible party, to external stakeholders including works councils, unions, labour inspectorates, and other government bodies, and to a P&O Workforce Strategy Head (global or local). The Country People Experience Head should support business leaders & P&O Workforce Strategy Heads, navigate these situations end to end. The Country head of People Experience will jointly assess together with the in-country P&O Workforce Strategy Head how certain local positions impact the local business strategies and execution and whether specific interventions are needed. The in-country P&O Workforce Strategy Head may lead the discussions with the local business leadership team to ensure streamlined communication to local leadership.

• Business & P&O Strategy Execution in Partnership The Country Head of People Experience is the execution leader of people experience strategy at the local level (covering all aspects of people experience across our key journeys and delivery of people products). And working in close partnership with Global or Local P&O Workforce Strategy Heads, to translate global business and P&O strategy into locally grounded, actionable people plans — and are accountable for the implementation and outcomes of that strategy in-country. The Country Head of People Experience also proactively engages with Local or Global P&O Workforce Strategy Heads in case he or she receives signals that business strategies are at risk due to specific execution challenges or business leader engagement. Together with the in-country P&O Workforce Strategy Head, this role co-creates the local P&O strategies that can be applied to all business units in that country. This is not advisory support to a P&O Workforce Strategy Heads; it is shared execution accountability. Where a major business initiative has people implications at country level — a new operating model, an M&A integration, an expansion into a new location, a significant headcount change — this role leads the local P&O workstream from planning through delivery.

• First Point of Contact for Country-Level P&O Escalations The Country Head of People Experience holds clear ownership of all P&O escalations that are country-specific in nature. Business leaders and the in-country P&O Workforce Strategy Heads do not need to navigate the global P&O structure to find the right person for a complex local matter — this role is that person. They diagnose the situation, apply local legal and regulatory expertise, coordinate with global product teams, P&O experts and Global P&O Workforce Strategy Heads where needed, and provide a clear resolution or recommendation. They ensure escalations are handled with speed, competence, and appropriate confidentiality — and that recurring patterns of escalation are fed back into product design or policy review so that systemic issues are addressed rather than repeatedly managed.

• Local Product Landing & Adoption The Country Head of People Experience is the primary accountability holder for how global P&O products are adopted and experienced in their country (where relevant) – for example when it comes to Rewards programs, employee benefits, payroll & time management, recruitment solutions, diversity & inclusion programs (illustrative, not exhaustive). They lead local change management for relevant P&O product launches or significant product change, building awareness, readiness, and momentum. They recruit and activate local champions — managers, employees, and team leads — who carry adoption into the organisation. They monitor adoption data, including usage of AI enabled technology, and act on it: where products are not being used or do not deliver required business outcomes / employee experience goals, they diagnose why and either address the local adoption gap or escalate a legitimate design issue to the Product Owner for improvement. In cases where there is a need for a local root cause analysis, this role is accountable to ensure end to end process fixes are put in place to avoid recurrence of the same issue.

• Local Context & Product Feedback This role is a critical intelligence feed for the global product teams. The Country Head of People Experience systematically gathers structured insight from employees, managers, and local P&O team members about what is working and what is creating friction in the lived experience or required business outcomes. They provide Product Owners with the local context — cultural norms, workforce composition, legal constraints, works council positions — that must inform product design and delivery.

• Compliance, Controls & Product Integrity The Country Head of People Experience owns compliance of global products against local legal standards. They ensure that every product is applied consistently and within the required local legal framework. Where a product cannot be applied as designed — for example where works council consultation requirements create mandatory process variations — they manage the exception with full transparency and documentation, ensuring this is the minimum necessary deviation, not a licence for broader non-compliance. They maintain the controls monitoring cadence for their country, flagging any control failures to the relevant Product Owner and Global Journey Head.

• Employee Relations & Works Council/Union Partnership The Country Head of People Experience is the organisation's accountable leader for all formal employee relations matters in the country. This includes works council and union relationships, collective agreement negotiations, handling of formal ER escalations, senior-level terminations, harassment and discrimination cases, and any ER matters that require legal or regulatory expertise.

• Local Legislation Advisory to P&O Workforce Strategy Heads & Business Leaders The Country Head of People Experience is the go-to authority on local employment law and regulatory requirements — for global and local Workforce Strategy Heads, for local business leaders, and for the wider P&O function. They advise on the country-specific legal or practice implications of workforce decisions — organisational changes, redundancies, cross-border moves, benefits structures, performance management approaches — ensuring that the business can act with confidence and without legal exposure. They do not own the strategic workforce decisions, which remain with P&O Workforce Strategy Heads and business leaders, but they own the legal and regulatory guardrails within which those decisions are made and flag proactively when strategy intentions may conflict with local law.

• Targeted Local P&O Programmes This role delivers specific and limited, non-standard activities that cannot be productised globally and must be designed and delivered in-country. These include local legally required initiatives, have very specific tax implications or are critical to achieve agreed business goals in that local market context, for example local employee benefits (as aligned with the P&O Workforce Strategy Heads guidance for their respective units. And the Country Head of People Experience will review the need & relevance of these programmes on a periodic basis with the aim to reduce them where possible.

• People Leadership of the Local P&O Team The Country Head of People Experience leads the local People Experience team and chairs the Country P&O Board. They set the direction, capability standards, and culture of the team. They ensure team members are actively connected into the global P&O product community — contributing local expertise to global product design rather than operating as a separate local function.

Skills & Knowledge (Capabilities the role requires)

Technical / Functional Capabilities:

• Local P&O Authority & Business Leadership Partnership. The most distinctive capability of this role. You are the trusted P&O authority for local business leaders across every dimension of the employment relationship — strategic, legal, cultural, and operational. Business leaders call you first because they know you will give them a clear, grounded, actionable perspective that reflects both business reality and local P&O expertise. You have the presence and credibility to operate as a genuine peer at the senior leadership table — not a service provider, but a strategic partner who shapes decisions. You are fluent in both English and the local language of the country you are based in.

• Strategy Translation & Local Execution Leadership. You take business and P&O strategy and make it real on the ground. You build country-level people plans that are specific, sequenced, and owned — and you are accountable for delivering them, not just advising on them. You work with Global and local P&O Workforce Strategy Heads as a co-execution partner, not as a downstream implementer, and you proactively identify where global strategy must be adapted to be executable locally. And you work closely with Global Product Owners and local teams to ensure P&O products deliver the right end to end experience and do not come across as highly fragmented and incoherent.

• Labor Relations & Employment Law Expertise. The bedrock specialist capability of this role. You are the organisation's in-country authority on employment legislation, collective agreements, and works council dynamics. You can negotiate in formal settings, advise on legal risk with confidence, and ensure that the organisation acts lawfully and fairly in every people decision. This capability cannot be standardised away — it is intrinsically local and intrinsically human.

• Escalation Handling & Judgment Under Complexity. You are the person who steps into difficult, ambiguous, or high-stakes situations and makes sound judgments quickly across all activities in the P&O lifecycle. You know how to triage an escalation — distinguishing between what can be resolved locally, what requires Expertise Hub or legal expertise, and what must be escalated further — and you ensure every situation is handled with appropriate urgency, discretion, and follow-through.

Leadership Capabilities:

• People Leadership & Local Team Development. You build a local P&O team that is connected, capable, and outward-facing — not a group of local administrators. You develop your team members' ability to engage with global products, contribute to product improvement, and operate as genuine consulting partners to local managers. You create clarity of purpose, a strong team culture, and career paths that extend into the wider P&O organisation. You also integrate specialist local expertise aligned to our global product teams (for example, in rewards, recruitment solutions, talent management etc.) into a coherent, high-performing team rather than a set of disconnected specialists.

• Stakeholder Trust Across Three Communities. You build and sustain trust with three distinct groups simultaneously: local business leaders and management who rely on your authority and expertise; the global P&O organisation — P&O Workforce Strategy Heads, Product Owners, Journey Leaders, and Expertise Hubs — who rely on your country intelligence and execution; and local employees, their representatives, and external parties who rely on your fairness, consistency, and integrity. Operating credibly across all three simultaneously is the defining capability tension of this role.

• Change Leadership & Adoption Driving. You are an expert change agent. You know how to translate a global product, policy, or business transformation into something that local managers and employees understand, believe in, and act on. You build trust before change arrives, create early adopters, celebrate visible wins, and diagnose adoption barriers quickly. You also lead the people workstream when the business is going through significant change in-country — ensuring that organizational transitions are well-managed, legally sound, and experienced as humanely as possible by the people affected.

Work Experience

• Proven track record of local P&O experience. The ideal candidate has country or regional HR experience and has interacted with local leaders, influenced decisions that impacted the experience of employees in that market, and implemented people plans that drove business outcomes.

• Strong ER and labour relations spine in the relevant country or region. Deep expertise in employment law and formal employee relations for the specific country is non-negotiable. This includes works council management, union negotiation experience, and senior ER case handling.

• Experience translating business and P&O strategy into local execution plans. The candidate has worked in a global-local model where they were responsible not just for advising on strategy but for implementing it — building country-level people plans, leading local workstreams in organizational change or transformation, and being accountable for delivery against agreed outcomes. They understand what it means to be the P&O execution lead for a business initiative, not just a stakeholder.

• Experience operating in a matrixed, global-local model. The candidate has operated in a large, globally managed organisation where products, standards, or policies were set centrally and had to be implemented locally. They have navigated the tension between global consistency and local necessity — advocating clearly, using evidence, and earning credibility with both central teams and local leaders without becoming a bottleneck or a point of friction.

• Change management and adoption experience. The candidate has led significant organizational or programme change, with demonstrable evidence of driving adoption rather than just communication. They understand that change management is a craft — not a cascade — and they have built local champions, identified resistance early, and adapted their approach based on adoption data.

• Track record of building trust as a first point of contact and escalation handler. The candidate has been the person business leaders, works councils, and employees turn to when a situation is complex, sensitive, or legally consequential. They have a track record of handling escalations with speed and judgment, and of building the kind of trust with business leaders that means they are included early — not called in after decisions have been made

• Track record of managing diverse local teams. The candidate has led a small-to-medium HR team with mixed specialisms and has developed the capability of team members over time, creating a culture of continuous improvement and connection to the broader organisation.

Skills Desired

Business Acumen, Change Management, Coaching, Data Analytics, Data-Driven Decision Making, Development Leadership, HR Strategy, Leadership, Organizational Design, Performance Management (PM), Stakeholder Management, Strategic Planning, Strategic Workforce Planning, Talent Management

• Accounts Receivable – monthly review of accounts receivable in the system and assist with the preparation of late notices and default notices.
• Assist Property Manager with the preparation of monthly/quarterly financial reports.
• Assist Property Manager with day-to-day operation of assigned portfolio.
• Assist with answering the main telephone line and screen calls to forward to the appropriate personnel; Deliver messages to personnel and/or forward messages to voicemail; Greet guests and notify personnel of incoming visitors; Accept deliveries/packages.
• Receive and enter work order requests into the system.
• Maintain, track, and input into the system all Certificates of Insurance for vendors/tenants/clients.
• Prepare, compile, and facilitate the creation and execution of Service Contracts for vendor services.
• Schedule building activity, including move-ins / move-outs; verify insurance.
• Assist in planning and executing tenant events with the management team.

• Bachelor’s Degree preferred
• Proficient with Microsoft Excel and Word; Yardi experience a plus

• Strong verbal and written communication skills
• Excellent customer service skills
• Good organizational skills

jobs.title: Construction Project Manager
jobs.description:
As a Construction Project Manager, your main focus will be to lead and manage construction projects end‑to‑end, ensuring they are delivered efficiently, professionally, and in full compliance with company standards, policies, quality requirements, and timelines. You oversee planning, budgeting, contracting, execution, documentation, and collaboration with internal and external partners to secure sustainable, safe, and cost‑efficient project outcomes.

This on-site role reports into our Construction Manager and is based out of one of our Sales Region locations (New York/LA/Houston/Miami)

A Day in the Life

Working at H&M means no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will include the following responsibilities*

Planning, Budgeting & Pre-Construction

• Prepare investment project budgets and business cases in line with global Construction Processes

• Conduct site surveys, perform value engineering, and prepare risk analyses to support decision‑making

• Develop detailed project plans based on input from internal teams and external consultants, optimizing timelines and reducing installation, labour and related costs

• Align with Leasing and Legal on contractual obligations and project demarcation

• Liaise with consultants and authorities to secure all required permits

• Continuously improve planning and follow‑up tools and share best practices across the team

• Apply retro planning using input from other departments and consultants to minimize installation, labor, and other costs

Procurement, Contracting & Partner Management

• Support (Procurements Specialist) with external partners sourcing

• Support the pre‑qualification of new contractors to maintain a strong, high‑quality supplier base

• Review contracts to ensure all project and country‑specific risks are covered and attach execution and payment schedules accordingly

• Ensure all contracts and appendices are approved and signed before any work begin

• Secure contractual obligations through qualitative contract management throughout the project lifecycle

• Ensure country‑specific risks are incorporated in contracts and that payment schedules follow legal/market norms

• Ensure that all contracts are stored and signed according to approval rights and governance rules

Project Execution, Quality and Health & Safety

• Secure that stores are designed and built in line with building specifications and interior guidelines

• Follow up on construction progress through site visits and project meetings, ensuring deadlines, quality standards and compliance are met

• Ensure Health & Safety requirements are in place and consistently followed

• Manage change orders, secure transparency in all project finances, and keep the project budget within approved forecasts

• Ensure invoices reflect contractual terms and that landlord contributions are followed up

Documentation, Handover & Collaboration

• Ensure project timelines are accurately updated in LIMA (Planon) to support internal planning and future benchmarking

• Secure complete documentation before, during and after the project, stored according to global guidelines

• Challenge change orders proactively and ensure financial transparency for all projects

• Follow up on payment of landlord contributions to ensure timely reimbursement

• Ensure a structured and qualitative handover to Facility Management

• Proactively share relevant information with other departments in a timely and structured way

• Collaborate regularly with cross‑functional teams, both giving and requesting feedback to identify improvement opportunities

Who You Are:

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business administration or similar

• Project Management certifications are meriting

• Supplier and contract management

• Good understanding of the field of construction and the ability to identify risks and opportunities in a retail environment

• Knowledge in MS Office

• Advanced English level

• Previous work experience from retail construction, facility management and/or real estate

• Experience within the project management field

• Experience from managing external suppliers and follow-up on contractual obligations

• Experience from working in a role with several stakeholders

• Work experience in large international organization is meriting

• You are communicative and supportive, with a consultative and creative mindset. You value teamwork, work methodically, and remain resilient and achievement-oriented, maintaining focus and drive even under pressure

Why You’ll Love Working at H&M

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position

You will be responsible to support and lead various aspects of the dV5 Manufacturing Line, primarily focused on testing processes. This position is highly collaborative, and strong communication/presentation skills are fundamental to successful partnerships with engineering, production and management teams.

Essential Job Duties

• Demonstrate ownership of various manufacturing processes, including assembly/test.
• Provide real-time (onsite) technical support for issues as they arrive.
• Resolve failures of varying complexity, which may be related to process, hardware or software. Identify root cause and implement solutions to improve manufacturability.
• Present data and proposals at project team meetings or wider audience forums.
• Provide critical DFM (Design For Manufacturability) input to development teams for software processes and electrical-based sub-assemblies.
• Develop & utilize understanding of system error codes, P values, UID test functions.
• Assist with execution of purges and other major quality control processes for production, when product defects are identified.
• Own and execute Production Process Qualifications (PPQ), for the manufacturing line. Assist with major PPQ (full line or factory) validations.
• Participate in project teams for CAPAs, MCF (design changes), EDF (field issues), root cause analysis, DPU reduction, process improvements, CAPAs, Cost reduction, etc.
• Establish good working relationships with close functions (Production, Quality Eng, Design Eng, Supplier Eng, etc.)
• Execute complex DMR/DHR, BOM, and traveler document changes with little oversight.
• Translate factory/production data into actions or recommendations for improvements, with understanding of: DPU, yield, CPk, trend charts
• Use statistical tools independently to drive data metric reporting and improvements.
• Participate in risk analysis project teams whose intentions are to identify compliance gaps that may affect yields and quality metrics. Understands implications of lifecycles, how they are used in product development.
• May occasionally informally mentor or supervise colleagues’ work (technicians, documentation specialists, junior engineers, interns)
• Performs other duties as required.

Required Education and Training

• BS degree in Computer Science/Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering or other similar field.

Required Skills and Experience

• 3+ years experience in a manufacturing or design-related role
• Basic engineering principles and analysis techniques
• Solid understanding of computer architecture.
• Solid understanding of computer networking and cloud-based computing
• Basic experience with software tools/scripting (eg. Matlab, Python, etc.)
• Strong communication skills, both written and verbal. Necessary to engage with technicians, production management, product development, planning, purchasing, regulatory, inspection, customer support and clinical marketing organizations.

• Advanced skills with desktop software applications (Excel, Powerpoint, Word, etc.)
• Basic knowledge of process controls, including Six-Sigma, CPk, etc.
• High level of personal initiative, including ownership and leadership, to influence product design to improve reliability, robustness and performance.
• Troubleshooting ability to systematically and effectively break down a system or process into subparts to identify failures and troubleshoot to component level.
• Knowledge and execution of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).
• Excellent documentation skills and high standards for instructional clarity/accuracy.
• High energy and genuine excitement to learn and get to the bottom of problems.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• MS degree in an engineering discipline listed above.
• Prior experience working in an FDA/ISO regulated environment.
• Prior experience with Documentation and production control systems: Agile, SAP, MES
• Prior experience in development of: Matlab, Python
• Demonstrated ability to effectively design experiments, solve problems and implement them in manufacturing
• Expert knowledge (black-belt) of process controls, including Six-Sigma, CPk, etc.
• Prior experience evaluating/managing suppliers, of both custom and COTS parts.
• Experience in Just-In-Time, Demand Flow Technology, and Lean Manufacturing techniques.

They will act as the liaison between customer service, operations, and the support team and will be responsible for superior customer satisfaction with adherence to customer SLAs and KPIs, as well as supporting account retention, at their service center. They will work with the Service Center Manager to ensure the location meets or exceeds environmental health, safety, and regulatory compliance, DOT regulations, production, and waste management goals. The Service Center Supervisor should have working knowledge of equipment types, which may include box trucks, vans, roll-offs, and tankers. The Service Center Supervisor should have an understanding of logistics, planning, and exceeding customers' expectations.Under the general guidance of the Senior Transportation Manager, the Service Center Supervisor will lead a team of people (may include drivers, driver assistants, and dispatchers) related to transportation at a Service Center to support operational strategies that align with the company’s culture and long-term goals to exceed our customers’ expectations. Leadership & Strategy

Active CDL is preferred.

• Experience using an integrated fleet, driver, and compliance management software. Experience with Samsara is a plus.

Skills: (The skills listed are the abilities and knowledge required to perform the job effectively.)

jobs.title: Reliability Engineer
jobs.description:
We are seeking a results-driven Reliability Engineer to join our Engineering & Maintenance team to support the maintenance and reliability efforts across fourteen coil coating facilities. This individual will be responsible for driving equipment reliability improvements, reducing downtime, and optimizing asset performance by applying engineering methodologies, data analysis, and continuous improvement strategies. The ideal candidate brings strong problem-solving skills, technical expertise in heavy manufacturing, and a passion for sustainable, cost-effective operations.

Key Responsibilities:

• Reliability Improvement:Lead root cause analysis (RCA) and failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) on critical equipment failures.Develop and implement proactive maintenance strategies, including preventive and predictive maintenance (PdM) programs.Monitor equipment performance metrics (MTBF, MTTR, OEE) and identify areas for reliability improvement.Assist facilities in managing critical spare parts programs.Assist facilities in the development and management of lubrication programs.
• Data Analysis & Reporting:Collect and analyze equipment and maintenance data to drive decision-making and track asset health.Utilize CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management Systems) and reliability tools (e.g., vibration analysis, thermography, oil analysis).
• Project Leadership:Lead reliability projects such as equipment upgrades, replacements, or process optimizations.Collaborate with operations, maintenance, and engineering teams across multiple plant sites to align on best practices and standardization.
• Asset Management:Support capital asset lifecycle management including design for reliability (DfR) and maintenance planning.Review and refine equipment specifications, PM routines, and critical spare part strategies.
• Training & Culture:Train maintenance personnel on condition monitoring and reliability-centered maintenance techniques.Foster a reliability-focused culture by promoting awareness and accountability at all organizational levels.Participate in the selection and introductory training of new plant maintenance leadership personnel

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial Engineering or related field required. Reliability certifications (e.g., CMRP, CRE) preferred.
• Experience: Minimum 7 years of reliability or maintenance engineering experience in heavy manufacturing (e.g., steel, cement, pulp & paper, mining, etc.). Multi-plant or multi-site experience is a strong plus.
• Technical Skills:Proficient in RCA, FMEA, RCM, and Six Sigma methodologies.Familiarity with PdM technologies (vibration, ultrasound, IR thermography).

If you’re passionate about sustainable design, cutting-edge HVAC systems, and want to help shape the future of high-performance buildings, we want to hear from you.

Why Join Us?

• Leadership role with autonomy and support — Build and lead your own team, with support from the executive level and peers.
• Work that matters — Design systems for complex, high-impact infrastructure in a way that will drive goals for electrification, carbon reduction, and energy performance.
• Broad opportunities for career growth and visibility — AECOM defines clear pathways of professional growth and leadership advancement.
• Collaboration — Join over 200 MEP professionals across the East Coast, plus over 700 New England multidisciplinary teammates, in a culture that values curiosity, respect, knowledge sharing and interdisciplinary problem-solving.
• Innovation — Champion new ways of delivering engineering excellence, including digital design tools, AI-enabled workflows, advanced simulation, and emerging approaches to sustainable building systems.

What You’ll Do:

• Lead and grow AECOM's building engineering practice in Boston, balancing technical excellence, team development, client service, and business performance.

• Develop and execute a strategic plan to expand local MEP capabilities and build an integrated, multidisciplinary engineering team.

• Drive major project pursuits — both stand-alone MEP/FP work and as part of larger multi-discipline teams.

• Represent AECOM to clients, participate in interviews, and help craft winning proposals.

Success in this role will be measured by team growth, employee engagement, technical quality, client satisfaction, and successful project delivery.

jobs.title: Account Manager
jobs.description:
About Vouch:

Vouch is the insurance broker that powers ambition.

We’re a tech-enabled insurance advisory and brokerage purpose-built for growing companies in technology, life sciences, and professional services. Our clients are ambitious leaders building complex businesses, and we help them manage risk with tailored advice, smart coverage, and responsive service.

Backed by over $200M from world-class investors, Vouch combines deep industry expertise with AI-powered tools to deliver a better insurance experience. Our digital workflows reduce friction, speed up decisions, and give our clients the confidence to move faster.

Why should you join our team and Vouch?

Not only is this an exciting and growing team where you can drive a real impact on our operational scalability, but Vouch is also the preferred insurance provider to customers of Y Combinator, Brex, Carta, and WeWork. We’re a quickly growing startup that believes in transparency and acknowledgment with our team members and cultivating a values-driven company. Our values are "Be Client Obsessed", "Own it together", "Act with integrity and empathy", "Stay Curious and Grow", and "Empower People."

What does a work environment look like at Vouch?
Vouch has employees located across the U.S., with offices in San Francisco, Chicago, and New York City. While this role has hybrid work flexibility, we require team members to be in the office at least three days per week (Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday) to foster close collaboration and team building.

Why this role matters:

As a Success team member, you will be responsible for ensuring our customers have a great experience after purchasing coverage with Vouch. This position will be responsible for guiding existing customers through any insurance questions they may have, day-to-day servicing of accounts, renewal business, supporting client needs when changing coverage, and ensuring a great experience for all Vouch customers.

We pride ourselves on making things fast, easy, and tailored for our customers. Some of our best customer feedback is about our amazing customer experience and service. You’ll be responsible for helping us scale that reputation.

What you'll do:

• Establish trusted relationships with our customers
• Retain existing Vouch clients during their renewal process
• Analyze existing insurance packages and evaluate risk
• Deliver consistent and timely follow-up in response to client requests and issues
• Manage growing accounts, including advising clients on risk solutions and selling more products
• Effectively use Direct Carrier and Wholesale Broker platforms to secure alternative quotes and manage existing policies, including the preparation and presentation of submissions
• Construct and present customized insurance packages to clients
• Ensure clients are comfortable with and able to utilize the tools/services available through the Vouch platform
• Drive additional value by identifying follow-up opportunities for Vouch
• Collaborate with billing and Policy Administration teams on client/carrier instructions and assist in collections as needed

About you:

• 2+ years of sales, brokerage, customer service, or other client-facing experience – within the insurance industry preferred
• Strong communication and organizational skills
• Able to be agile and thrive in a fast-paced environment
• Possess a competitive drive to outperform peers and continuously improve hard and soft skills
• Dependable, positive, and detail-oriented with excellent follow-through skills
• Active/Current Property and Casualty License
• Ability to drive success through ambiguous and complex situations
• Takes initiative to problem solve when meeting resistance

Nice to have:

• Exposure to and passion for early-stage startups and/or high-growth environments
• A background in insurance or other regulated categories
• Prior experience in a quota-carrying role with responsibility for achieving individual quantitative goals

Vouch provides several benefits to help you bring your best self to work:

• 💰 Competitive compensation and equity packages
• ⚕️ Health, dental, and vision insurance
• 🍼 Parental leave
• 🌴 Flexible vacation time
• 🪷 Wellness allowance
• 🛜 Technology allowance
• 📚 Company-sponsored personal and professional development
• 🏫 L&D: Partnerships with Ethena and monthly Lunch & Learns
• 🧘 Wellbeing: access to many wellbeing perks, including Peloton, Fetch, OneMedical, Headspace care+, etc.
• 🤗 Caregiver Support: company seed into the dependent care FSA and company sponsored Care.com membership.
• 📊 Regular performance reviews: Vouch conducts regular performance discussions with all team members, offering goal setting and check-ins, development discussions, and promotion opportunities.

What to expect in a typical interview process:

(Please note these steps may vary slightly depending on the role)

• 30 - 45 minute phone call with our recruiting team
• Case study/technical screen
• 45 minute video interview with the hiring manager
• Executive chat

Compensation philosophy:

The On Target Earnings (OTE) for this role are $90,000 - $95,000 per year depending on experience.

($65,000 - $70,000 base salary + $25,000 variable annual compensation)

The base salary listed in the job posting represents what you can expect to earn on an annualized basis. This role is hourly and non-exempt, with overtime eligibility for hours worked over 40 in a week.

Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and industry and are part of our total compensation package, which also includes benefits and other perks. We also include stock options in all compensation packages and believe all Vouch employees should have the opportunity to become owners in the company. Individual pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, skill set, location, and business need. The pay range provided is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

Perform transactional duties to serve members with high accuracy in accordance with credit union policies and procedures as well as adhering to STCU’s balancing standards and proper dual control.

Job Experience: Minimum two years' experience as a Teller, new accounts or service representative in a financial institution required. Work Conditions: Exposure to constant or intermittent sounds at a low or moderate level consistent with an office setting. Exposure to high-stress, fast-paced, deadline-oriented environment.

• Must be able to read, write and speak the English language

Strategic Planning & Program Management

At Intuitive, we believe that minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care. Through ingenuity and intelligent technology, we expand the potential of physicians to heal without constraints. The Global Expansion Manager plays a critical role in enabling our vision by driving the successful and accelerated commercialization of products within the assigned region. Acting as the Directly Responsible Individual (DRI), the role bridges global product teams and local stakeholders—removing barriers, identifying accelerators, and enabling market readiness that advances patient access and Intuitive’s long-term growth.

jobs.title: Digital Asset Management (DAM) Solutions Architect - AI
jobs.description:
We are seeking a Digital Asset Management (DAM) Solutions Architect to lead the design, configuration, integration, and evolution of digital asset management capabilities supporting modern content operations and AI-enabled content workflows.

This role sits at the intersection of technology architecture, content operations, information architecture, and digital publishing. The ideal candidate combines hands-on knowledge of enterprise DAM platforms with a strong understanding of taxonomy, metadata, digital rights, content lifecycle management, publishing requirements, and integration with upstream and downstream enterprise systems.

The DAM Solutions Architect will help translate business and content requirements into scalable DAM solutions—including metadata models, taxonomy structures, asset organization, workflow, governance, publishing patterns, and system integrations.

This role will also help establish DAM and content-management standards that enable content to be discoverable, reusable, interoperable, governed, and consumable by both human users and AI-enabled platforms and workflows.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Our employees are tasked with delivering excellent business results through the efforts of their teams.  These results are achieved by:

DAM Architecture & Configuration

• Design and configure enterprise DAM solutions aligned to business, content, publishing, and technology requirements.
• Define asset structures, content models, folder and collection strategies, permissions, workflows, renditions, and lifecycle rules.
• Assess existing DAM implementations and identify opportunities to improve scalability, usability, governance, and interoperability.
• Translate business and content-management requirements into functional and technical DAM specifications.
• Establish patterns supporting modular content, source assets, derivatives, channel-specific renditions, and packaged digital deliverables.
• Support migration and onboarding of existing content and assets into DAM environments.

Taxonomy, Metadata & Information Architecture

• Design and maintain scalable metadata schemas, taxonomies, controlled vocabularies, and tagging strategies.
• Establish standards for descriptive, structural, operational, technical, compliance, attribution, and rights-management metadata.
• Define relationships between asset-level attributes, taxonomy values, keywords, tags, and other content classifications.
• Develop metadata strategies that improve search, discovery, reuse, automation, and reporting.
• Establish approaches for capturing AI-related content provenance and attribution, including generated or AI-modified content where applicable.
• Ensure metadata and taxonomy models can evolve as new brands, markets, channels, content types, and use cases are introduced.

Content Lifecycle, Governance & Digital Rights

• Define and document content and asset lifecycle processes from creation and approval through publication, reuse, expiration, archival, and retirement.
• Establish governance standards for metadata quality, taxonomy management, asset stewardship, and content hygiene.
• Design approaches for managing digital rights, including licensing, usage restrictions, geography, channel, talent, expiration, and other rights-related attributes.
• Partner with content operations and business stakeholders to define roles and responsibilities for ongoing DAM governance and asset stewardship.
• Help establish operating models for DAM administrators, content owners, librarians, and other asset-management roles.

Digital Publishing & Content Supply Chain

• Understand digital publishing requirements across web, email, social, media, CRM, and other digital channels.
• Define requirements for asset transformation, renditions, packaging, distribution, and downstream consumption.
• Design DAM capabilities supporting modular and omnichannel content operations.
• Ensure DAM architecture supports the movement of assets throughout the content supply chain—from creation and approval through publishing and activation.
• Partner with creative, content, marketing operations, and technology teams to establish scalable publishing patterns.

Systems Integration

• Design integration patterns between DAM platforms and upstream/downstream enterprise systems.
• Define APIs, events, webhooks, metadata mappings, authentication requirements, asset-transfer patterns, and integration contracts.
• Support integration with systems such as:Content creation and design platformsContent management systems (CMS)Marketing workflow/project-management platformsMedical/legal/regulatory review and approval platformsClaims-management solutionsCRM and marketing automation platformsOmnichannel orchestration and activation platformsAI-enabled content-generation and content-management solutions
• Define appropriate integration triggers, audit requirements, exception handling, retry processing, and operational monitoring.
• Work closely with engineering teams to translate architectural designs into implementation-ready specifications.

AI-Enabled Content Operations

• Help design DAM capabilities that support AI-enabled content generation, retrieval, reuse, and automation.
• Establish metadata and content structures that enable assets to provide reliable context to AI applications and agents.
• Define approaches for distinguishing and governing human-created, AI-generated, and AI-modified content.
• Partner with AI/product teams to establish integration patterns between DAM platforms and AI-enabled content platforms.
• Identify opportunities to use AI to improve tagging, classification, metadata enrichment, asset discovery, and content operations while maintaining appropriate governance and human oversight.

MINIMUM KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

The requirements listed below are representative of the experience, education, knowledge, skill and/or abilities required.

• Significant experience designing, implementing, configuring, or architecting enterprise Digital Asset Management solutions.
• Strong understanding of DAM taxonomy, metadata architecture, controlled vocabularies, tagging, and information architecture.
• Experience with enterprise DAM platforms such as Adobe Experience Manager Assets / Adobe Assets, Aprimo, Bynder, Acquia DAM, Sitecore Content Hub, or comparable platforms.
• Strong understanding of digital content lifecycle management and content supply-chain processes.
• Experience designing integrations using REST APIs, events, webhooks, middleware, and related enterprise integration patterns.
• Understanding of digital publishing requirements across multiple channels and content formats.
• Experience with asset renditions, transformations, derivatives, packaging, and distribution.

• Experience collaborating across business, creative, content operations, product, engineering, and technology teams.

At the Suites of Someren Glen, we believe our community thrives when our care partners are happy and empowered to give their best. If you have experience in long-term care or memory care and a real passion for working with older adults, we’d love to meet you.

jobs.title: Senior Principal Pathologist
jobs.description:
Job Description

The primary function is to assess the safety of experimental compounds by evaluating their effects across available nonclinical safety models. Act as a scientific subject matter expert for preclinical safety data for other AbbVie departments as a member of cross-functional project teams. Develop and conduct those portions of study protocols that deal with anatomic and clinical pathology including not only the collection and evaluation of data regarding gross, microscopic, ultra-structural, and clinical pathology but, lastly, the preparation of comprehensive reports correlating these data. Integrate data sourced from in vivo studies as well as in vitro models and in silico predictions to generate a comprehensive safety assessment for early drug development programs.

Responsibilities

• Provide scientific expertise to scientific staff of other departments as a member of cross-functional teams.
• In cooperation with the Toxicology Department, design, direct, and evaluate in vivo studies to determine the potential toxicity of experimental compounds in different species of animals. This includes advanced endpoints (molecular pathology, ultrastructure, imaging, -omics, etc)
• Integrates the anatomic pathology data, clinical pathology data and other study findings to generate a pathology report as a component of the Toxicology report.
• Partner with toxicologists, pathologists and other functions to develop optimal strategies to address specific toxicology issues as well as select and advance Development compounds.
• Ability to function in multidisciplinary teams to address regulatory queries.
• Serves and/or leads issue resolution teams and participates in due diligence teams.
• Responsible for compliance with applicable Corporate and Divisional Policies and procedures.

Qualifications

• Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM or equivalent) plus post graduate training in veterinary pathology.
• Board Certification in Veterinary Anatomic Pathology (ACVP or equivalent) strongly preferred.
• Candidates with a Ph.D. in pathology or related discipline are strongly preferred.
• Familiarity with related fields: pharmacology, toxicology and drug development.
• Seasoned experience in biological research, supervisory abilities, and the ability to work effectively with other people.

jobs.title: Senior Staff Product Management
jobs.description:
We are seeking a Sr. Staff Strategic Capacity PM to own long-term capacity gap identification, provide solution proposals, and lead the initiatives to solve capacity constraints. This role will develop integrated demand/capacity models, maintain internal and external supply chain capacity profiles by site, support surge planning, and lead constraint engineering to identify and solve hidden systemic bottlenecks early enough to align capacity, cost, and DFM actions before NPI start and production ramp.

The ideal candidate combines strong quantitative modeling skills, semiconductor supply chain knowledge, constraint engineering discipline, and program management experience to deliver predictable capacity availability at scale, reduce late capacity escalations, prevent surprise bottlenecks at ramp, and connect capacity investment and qualification roadmaps to business needs.

Renesas Electronics, a leading global semiconductor company, is rapidly scaling its AI-focused power delivery business. Products include high-performance digital power VRMs, multiphase controllers, Smart Power Stages (SPS), Vertical Power Stages (SPS with integrated capacitors and multiple silicon die), Power Towers (power modules integrating multiple SPS-equivalents with capacitors and inductors), and power MOSFETs.

Key Responsibilities

Long-term Demand & Capacity Modeling

• Develop and maintain component-level demand/capacity models across product lines, technology nodes, manufacturing flows, and planning horizons.

• Build scenario-based models for base, upside, downside, and surge demand to support executive capacity decisions.

• Establish planning assumptions, model governance, and refresh cadence to improve forecast consistency and decision quality.

Supply Chain Capacity Profiles & Constraint Management

• Create and maintain supply chain capacity profiles across internal and external manufacturing sites, including front-end, back-end, test, and critical supplier constraints.

• Identify structural capacity constraints early and define mitigation paths before NPI start or production ramp commitments.

• Support surge planning by modeling practical upside capacity, recovery timing, qualification dependencies, and risk buffers.

• Drive fewer late capacity escalations by converting long-range signals into actionable capacity readiness plans.

Constraint Engineering & Systemic Bottleneck Resolution

• Identify hidden systemic bottlenecks across design, manufacturing, test, supplier capability, yield, cost, and capacity interfaces before they impact ramp execution.

• Lead data-driven root cause analysis using operational, engineering, supplier, yield, and cycle-time data to isolate constraint drivers and quantify business impact.

Program Management

• Program Manage the constraint resolution initiatives from detection through mitigation, closure, and recurrence prevention across cross-functional teams.

• Feed structural fixes into DFM, capacity planning, cost reduction, qualification, and supplier readiness roadmaps.

• Mitigate systemic scaling failures by converting recurring bottlenecks into durable process, design, sourcing, or capacity solutions.

• Facilitate cross-functional capacity reviews to align demand signals, site readiness, supplier capability, and qualification plans.

Risk Management & Analytics

• Conduct sensitivity analysis on demand volatility, supplier constraints, site readiness, surge scenarios, and systemic scaling risks.

• Drive continuous improvement in modeling methods, data quality, and planning tools to improve capacity predictability at scale.

• Improve recovery speed from issues that do occur by establishing decision paths, mitigation playbooks, and feedback loops into capacity and DFM planning.

• Bachelor’s degree in Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, or related field.

• 7+ years of experience in semiconductor manufacturing, supply chain planning, or operations strategy.

• Strong understanding of semiconductor fabrication and supply chain with Program Management leadership experience.

• Experience identifying systemic bottlenecks, leading data-driven root cause analysis, and driving solutions across engineering, manufacturing, supplier and planning teams.

• Advanced analytical and modeling skills (Excel, VCO, AI Optimization, SQL, Python, or similar tools).

• Excellent communication and presentation skills.

Preferred

• MBA or Master’s degree in Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain or related field.

• Strong stakeholder management, communication, collaboration, and partnership skills across Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and OSAT partners.

• Familiarity with statistical forecasting methods.

• Knowledge of industry cycles and long-lead semiconductor equipment planning.

Key Competencies

• Strategic thinking with strong data analytics acumen

• Data-driven decision making

• Scenario modeling and financial analysis

• Cross-functional leadership

• Risk assessment and mitigation

• Constraint engineering and systemic bottleneck resolution

Renesas is an embedded semiconductor solution provider driven by its Purpose, To Make Our Lives Easier. With a global team of over 21,000 engineers and problem solvers in more than 30 countries, we offer the opportunity to work on world‑leading technology for Automotive, Industrial, Infrastructure, and IoT, shaping a safer, healthier, greener, and smarter future.

This position brings an opportunity to make innovative contributions that will define how AbbVie leverages AI-enabled drug discovery across our small molecule portfolio. The key responsibilities of this position are to identify, develop, optimize, validate, and deploy innovative machine learning approaches to guide molecular optimization. This role will collaborate closely with project teams comprising medicinal chemists, structural biologists, biochemists, cell biologists, and other computational chemistry / chemoinformatics experts.

Responsibilities:

• Consult with project team to establish quantitative targets for driving optimization
• Identify suitable models to predict small molecule binding affinities for protein targets, and to predict pharmacological properties (PK parameters, etc.)
• Build predictive models for each project endpoint, and carefully benchmarking to evaluate performance and domain of applicability for each model
• Decisively identify the model that should be used for each project team query molecule, using data-driven approaches that take account of model uncertainty and heteroscedasticity
• Clearly communicate to the project team the rationale for model selection and why the selected models are best suited for the task at hand
• Deploy models to ensure accessibility for the project team, facilitating collaborative ideation and optimization

• Senior Scientist I: Degree in relevant field (chemistry / computer science / machine learning / cheminformatics / chemical engineering) with experience developing machine learning models related to chemical and biological data (10+ years of experience for BS, 8+ years for MS, 0+ years for PhD). Leveling will be commensurate to experience.
• Senior Scientist II: Degree in relevant field (chemistry / computer science / machine learning / cheminformatics / chemical engineering) with experience developing machine learning models related to chemical and biological data (12+ years of experience for BS, 10+ years for MS, 4+ years for PhD). Leveling will be commensurate to experience.
• Expertise with developing, implementing and deploying programs and computational solutions employing Machine Learning/Deep learning and Cheminformatics
• Expertise in AI/ML-enabled molecular generation, pose prediction, affinity prediction and/or prediction of pharmacological properties (e.g. PK)
• Strong programming skills in Python and experience with data science stack including numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, and other related scientific libraries
• Ability to implement, debug, and maintain computational tools in common programming languages (Python, etc…) and proficiency with cloud computing capabilities
• Familiarity with modern deep learning architectures including GNN, CNN, RNN, Transformer, GCNN and MPNN, and machine learning paradigms such as generative models, GAN, and active learning
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with demonstrated ability to think critically and creatively, and provide solutions both individually and collaboratively with internal experts
• Excellent ability to communicate clearly and concisely with colleagues and collaborators including an ability to explain complex ideas to non-specialists

jobs.title: Senior Key Account Manager
jobs.description:
The Senior Key Account Manager is responsible for managing and developing the assigned portfolio of operators in their territory, ensuring active commercial presence, strong client relationships and sustained revenue growth for Evolution in each account. This role combines the management of existing accounts with the identification of upselling opportunities, the execution of the local commercial strategy and direct operator support across Evolution's full product portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Client Portfolio Management

• Manage a selected number of high-priority strategic accounts that require senior-level engagement, long-term relationship building and a highly personalised commercial approach.
• Lead strategic reviews, negotiations and growth planning for these accounts.
• Serve as the senior commercial point of contact for these clients.
• Act as the primary point of contact for operators on all commercial matters: product, promotions, performance and issue resolution.
• Conduct regular meetings with each operator to review performance, identify opportunities and align strategies.
• Ensure that no operator in the portfolio is left without appropriate commercial attention.

Growth & Upselling

• Identify growth opportunities within the portfolio — new products, dedicated tables, exclusive content and promotional mechanics.
• Propose and negotiate initiatives with operators that expand Evolution's presence within their platform.
• Monitor KPIs for each account and identify early signals of risk or growth potential.
• Support the negotiation and sale of dedicated tables, coordinating internally with the Commercial Team Manager and product team.

Commercial Policy & Pricing

• Apply Evolution's commercial guidelines and pricing policy across all accounts in the assigned portfolio.
• Ensure that commercial conditions agreed with each operator are consistent with the regional strategy and properly documented.

Commercial Execution

• Execute the commercial strategy defined by the Commercial Team Manager within each account in the portfolio.
• Coordinate with Product, Promotions, Integrations and Marketing teams to ensure operators have the materials, tools and support they need.
• Manage the commercial onboarding of newly assigned operators, ensuring a fast and smooth activation.
• Maintain an updated pipeline and report regularly to the Commercial Team Manager on portfolio status.

Reporting & Planning

• Report to the Commercial Team Manager on portfolio performance, opportunities, risks and market developments.
• Contribute to the territory commercial planning process with a grounded view of each account's growth potential.
• Use the team's commercial tools consistently and keep all information up to date.

The duties and responsibilities described in this job description are not a comprehensive list and as such additional tasks may be assigned to the employee from time to time; The scope of the job may also be subject to change as necessitated by business demands.

• Minimum of 1 year of experience in a similar role
• B2B experience is required
• Advanced English proficiency
• Spanish is required
• Strong data analysis skills
• Proficiency in Jira and Excel
• Market experience in similar roles is highly valued

jobs.title: Pre-K Part-Time Aftercare Support - Crown Heights
jobs.description:
The Enrichment & Pre-K Aftercare Support Aide plays a vital role in supporting student safety, behavior management, and active engagement across multiple grade levels. Working part-time, Monday through Friday from 12:30 PM to 5:00 PM, this role bridges elementary enrichment instruction and early childhood aftercare support. From 12:30 PM to 3:00 PM, the Aide supports our Elementary School (K-2) Enrichment Dance program. From 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM, the Aide transitions to leading supervision and structured activities for our Pre-K aftercare program.

jobs.title: Principal Fellow
Construction Inspector
jobs.description:
As a Construction Inspector, you will provide on-site inspection, monitoring, reporting and documentation for municipal infrastructure projects, including water/ wastewater treatment facility, water distribution piping, sanitary sewers, and roadway construction. In this role, you will help ensure that work is completed in accordance with approved plans, specifications, and regulatory standards while supporting project managers and engineers throughout the construction process.

This is a 24 month temporary contract position with the potential for extension.

Responsibilities include:

• Perform daily field inspections of civil infrastructure construction
• Monitor contractor activities for compliance with project plans, specifications, and municipal standards.
• Document daily construction activities, quantities, and site conditions using inspection reports and photo logs.
• Observe and verify materials, testing procedures, and workmanship.
• Coordinate with contractors, engineers, utility providers, and municipal staff to resolve field issues.
• Assist with reviewing shop drawings, RFIs, and change orders as needed.
• Monitor health and safety compliance on-site
• Ensure compliance with safety regulations and environmental requirements. Participate in project meetings and provide progress updates.

Minimum Requirements:

• 6+ years of experience in construction inspection for municipal civil infrastructure.
• Understanding of water, sanitary, storm, and roadway construction methods and materials.
• Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and standards.

Preferred Qualifications:

• 8+ years of experience in construction inspection for municipal civil infrastructure.
• Engineering Technologist Certification
• Prior health and safety experience
• Proficiency with inspection documentation tools (e.g., tablets, daily logs, photo documentation).
• Familiarity with municipal codes, public works standards, and construction best practices.
• Strong communication and problem‑solving skills.
• Valid driver’s license and ability to work outdoors in varying conditions.

jobs.title: Pre-K Apprentice Teacher
jobs.description:
Uncommon Pre-K Teachers cultivate a love for learning in every student from the very start. Our teachers and students engage in a learning environment that fosters curiosity, achievement, respect, and empathy (CARE). Our classrooms are engaging, intentional and playful.  We have built a community where teachers encourage our core values of respect and hard work while celebrating the uniqueness of each student and laying the academic foundations that carry students to and through college. Our classrooms are led by teaching teams that consist of a lead teacher and apprentice teacher.

Instruction

• You’ll co-teach and build an engaging and joyful classroom environment that encourages mastery and empowers students to learn through exploration and purposeful play.
• You’ll co-teach literacy (phonics, language development, vocabulary, and writing), mathematics, core knowledge (science and social studies).
• The teaching team (lead & apprentice teachers) work together to facilitate our free-choice centers and small group instruction.

Data Analysis

• You'll meet weekly with your director to analyze and respond to trends in student work samples and assessments.
• You'll learn and implement strategies to differentiate instruction for all learners in your classroom.

Classroom Culture

• Implement instructional model and collaborate with instructional coach/director to ensure students are achieving academic goals
• Use multiple data sources (assessments, classroom quality observations, and other data collections) to make day-by-day decisions about instruction (reflective)
• Provide early-learning experiences that contribute to children’s positive feelings about school, teachers, and their communities (nurturing)
• Support children’s development across social-emotional, physical, cognitive, and academic competencies (balanced)
• Apply a variety of strategies to promote both concept and skill development
• Provide modeling and support for children’s expressive and receptive language throughout the school day

School Culture

• You’ll build positive relationships with students to ensure they feel seen, loved, and heard.
• You’ll partner with students’ families to ensure appropriate resources are available to support their children’s learning needs.
• You'll engage in practice-based professional development, mentorship, and coaching sessions.
• You’ll support morning arrival, lunch duty, student assemblies, class transitions, and after-school dismissal.
• You'll participate in weekly, school-wide meetings to foster community, model our core values, and encourage student achievement.
• You'll partner with your teaching partner and grade level team to develop academic goals and practice instructional strategies.

• Drive to improve the minds and lives of students in and out of the classroom
• Evidence of self-motivation, willingness to be a team player, and has a strong sense of personal responsibility;
• Ideal candidates are hard-working, urgent, energetic, and are willing to learn and adapt;
• Is extremely reflective and constantly wants to improve;
• is flexible and enjoys dealing with unpredictability;
• Strong time management skills; ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and meet tight deadlines;
• A strong candidate will possess strong organizational skills, communication skills (particularly with children), and problem solving skills;
• Interest in performing a critical support role and the ability to excel in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial, results-oriented environment;
• Prior experience working in schools and/or urban communities is preferred but not required;
• Relentless commitment to mission of educating urban students. Belief in and alignment with Uncommon’s core beliefs and educational philosophy is non-negotiable.

jobs.title: Senior Staff Segment Strategy Manager – Industrial Applications
jobs.description:
The Segment Strategy Manager is responsible for defining and driving the system solution portfolio strategy for Industrial and Building and Home Applications. Working closely with global Application and Technology Architects and regional Solution Marketing teams, this role identifies market opportunities, translates customer needs into solution concepts, develops investment business cases, monitors solution development, drives solution commercialization, and owns the execution of approved solution opportunities from concept through successful market adoption.

The role serves as the market-facing counterpart to the architecture teams, ensuring that solution investments are aligned with customer requirements, technology roadmaps, and business objectives. It acts as the focal point between regional Solution Marketing teams, Product Groups, Architecture teams, Engineering, and Digital Marketing throughout the complete solution lifecycle. The role is accountable for driving cross-functional execution, stakeholder alignment, and achievement of approved business objectives throughout the solution lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities

Segment Strategy & Market Intelligence

• Analyze market trends, customer needs, competitive dynamics, and emerging technologies within the assigned segment.
• Identify growth opportunities, priority applications, and key use cases.
• Develop market assessments, business forecasts, and segment solution roadmaps.
• Define solution portfolio priorities and investment recommendations aligned with segment growth objectives.

Solution Opportunity Management

• Gather, evaluate, and prioritize solution opportunities from regional teams, product groups, customers, and ecosystem partners.
• Collaborate with Application and Technology Architects to define solution concepts and assess technical feasibility.
• Own assigned solution opportunities from initial evaluation through commercialization.
• Drive alignment and execution across all stakeholders required to successfully deliver approved solution initiatives.
• Prioritize opportunities based on market potential, strategic value, business impact, and portfolio fit.

Business Case Development

• Develop business cases and investment proposals for new system solutions.
• Assess market opportunity, revenue potential, costs, risks, and expected returns.
• Define solution success metrics and commercialization objectives.
• Develop investment recommendations and prioritization proposals for management approval

Development Governance & Approval

• Prepare development approval packages and executive presentations.
• Drive alignment across Architecture, Engineering, Product Groups, Marketing, Sales, and Finance.
• Support management reviews and investment decision processes.
• Own execution readiness, ensuring resources, stakeholder commitments, and business objectives remain aligned throughout the approval process.

Solution Development Leadership

• Oversee solution development from concept to launch.
• Represent customer and market requirements throughout the development lifecycle.
• Track progress against business objectives, milestones, and market requirements.
• Act as the business owner and execution leader for approved solution initiatives.
• Drive issue resolution, risk mitigation, and cross-functional decision making to maintain execution momentum.
• Escalate resource, priority, or execution risks when required to achieve approved business objectives.

Go-to-Market & Commercialization

• Coordinate solution launch activities with Digital Marketing, Regional Solution Marketing, Product Groups, and Sales teams.
• Support development of value propositions, marketing collateral, demonstrations, and customer-facing materials.
• Monitor solution adoption, market impact, and launch effectiveness.
• Partner with regional teams and key customers to validate solution value propositions and commercialization plans.
• Monitor post-launch performance and drive corrective actions when business objectives are not achieved.

Key Interfaces

Internal Stakeholders

• Application Architects
• Technology Architects
• Product Groups
• Engineering Organizations
• Regional Solution Marketing Teams
• Digital Marketing
• Sales and Business Development
• Finance
• Executive Leadership Team

External Stakeholders

• Customers
• Strategic Partners
• Technology Ecosystem Partners
• Industry Associations
• Research Institutions and Universities

• 8+ years of experience in Product Marketing, Segment Marketing, Product Management, Business Development, or Solution Management.
• Strong understanding of system-level solutions and technology-driven markets.
• Experience developing business cases and investment proposals.
• Demonstrated track record of leading complex cross-functional initiatives from concept through commercialization.
• Ability to work effectively across global cross-functional organizations.
• Excellent presentation and executive communication skills.

Critical Competencies

• Strategic Thinking
• Market Analysis
• Business Case Development
• Solution Portfolio Management
• Project / Program Management
• Technology and Application Understanding
• Cross-Functional Leadership
• Stakeholder Management

Success Metrics

• Number and quality of approved solution investments
• Business case ROI achievement
• Solution adoption and design wins
• Time-to-market of solutions
• Portfolio health and strategic alignment
• Customer and stakeholder satisfaction

jobs.title: High School Science Teacher
jobs.description:
Uncommon High School Science teachers work collaboratively across the network to prepare all students with the tools and knowledge to critically engage in the field of science and develop them into self-directed learners. At the heart of all Science courses is inquiry-based learning, including a robust focus on student discourse and the science practices. Science teachers employ a variety of instructional strategies to develop a passion for scientific questioning and analysis in their students. Our teachers prepare all students such that they have the choice to study and excel in any STEM discipline. We prepare all students to be citizen scientists that have the tools and knowledge to critically engage in the field of science regardless of their university major or professional career. Our teachers become experts in their course content and have a keen sense of how to motivate and inspire high school students.

Responsibilities

1.     Instruction

• You’ll teach a curriculum that includes, but is not limited to, analysis of Biology, Chemistry, Physics, and Environmental Sciences that prepares students for Advanced Placement (AP) and collegiate level coursework.
• You'll develop students’ practices skills of questioning, modeling, constructing explanations, data analysis, argumentation, and planning and conducting interactive labs.
• You’ll create an environment where students feel confident using their voice to engage in scientific discourse.

Uncommon High School AP Capstone teachers are passionate about research and building an engaging, rigorous classroom culture focusing on helping all students gain the skills they need for college. Our teachers become experts in their course content, and have a keen sense of how to motivate and inspire high school students. At the heart of our AP Capstone classes is an emphasis on skill-building, communication and collaboration. Teachers facilitate student-directed research projects, building confidence in students to take on increasingly complex projects. At the conclusion of the AP Capstone program at Uncommon students will have planned, conducted, and presented their own research leaving them more prepared for the academic rigor and independence of college coursework.

• You’ll develop students’ independent and collaborative reading, writing, and discussion skills through several long term individual and group assignments.

You will research the right contacts, craft personalized outreach across channels, multi-thread into target accounts, and set the meetings that put our AEs in front of the decision-makers we need to be talking to.

This role works shoulder-to-shoulder with leadership, our AEs, and our Client Success team. You will have a direct hand in shaping how Actuate sells as we scale, and a clear, well defined path into an Account Executive role for the BDR who wants to grow.

Key Responsibilities

• Track and report key activity and outcome metrics including account penetration, meetings booked, opportunities created, and pipeline contribution
• Stay current on our verticals, our solutions, and our ICPs, so every conversation lands
• Represent Actuate professionally in every external interaction

Required Qualifications

• 2+ years of experience in business development, sales development, or related outbound roles, ideally in B2B SaaS, energy, IoT, or technology
• Demonstrated success running outbound into named accounts (not just spraying a list) with a track record of booking quality meetings
• Comfort using AI-assisted tools for research, personalization, and outreach, and curiosity about how to get more out of them
• Strong communication skills with the ability to engage senior decision-makers confidently by phone, email, and on social channels
• Hands-on experience with HubSpot (or a comparable CRM) and prospecting tools such as TitanX, Apollo, and LinkedIn Sales Navigator
• Sharp organizational skills and attention to detail managing many accounts and cadences at once
• Self-motivated, persistent, and coachable, with a real desire to learn the craft of selling
• Passion for technology and energy efficiency, and the impact our platform has on how buildings are run
• Comfortable in a fast-paced, collaborative startup environment where roles flex and ownership is expected

Preferred Qualifications
